QuestionStmt.S: The pH of a sample of vinegar is 3.76. Calculate the concentration of hydrogen ion in it in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$?

Solution.S:
Given pH = 3.76. The hydrogen ion concentration is found using $[\mathrm{H}^+] = 10^{-\text{pH}}$.

$$[\mathrm{H}^+] = 10^{-3.76} = 10^{-4 + 0.24} = 10^{-4} \times 10^{0.24}$$

The value of $10^{0.24}$ is approximately 1.7378. Therefore,
$$[\mathrm{H}^+] = 1.7378 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{mol dm}^{-3}$$

Rounding to three decimal places gives $1.738 \times 10^{-4}$. Hence, the correct option is B.
